The stability redesign. JDownloader's dark theme no longer fights the application it lives in — every fragile mechanism from the earlier lines has been replaced with an official API, a ground-truth signal, or an empirically verified flow, and the container is ad-free out of the box.

## ✨ Added

- **Ad-free by default.** JDownloader's built-in advertisements are switched off out of the box: the bottom **"Become premium user" banner**, the **premium-alert** column nags, the status-bar **"+ premium"** button, and the **special-deal** popups. Only advertisements are touched — the Donate button and every functional setting are left exactly as you set them. The flags live in `org.jdownloader.settings.GraphicalUserInterfaceSettings` (e.g. `bannerenabled`) and are re-applied on each start so a JDownloader self-update can't quietly bring the ads back.
- `JD_SELFUPDATE` (opt-in freeze) — `JD_SELFUPDATE=false` disables JD's periodic self-update checks for a frozen-appliance setup. Default stays `true`, since the same update channel delivers the hoster plugins, which go stale within weeks and break downloads. The first install (and the theme extension install) always use the updater regardless.
- **Silent headless pre-install, zero dialogs.** On a fresh install the whole JDownloader install chain now runs headless first — where no GUI exists, no forced installer dialog can appear. The FlatLaf theme extension is pre-requested in JD's update registry (`flatlaf-themes`), so it installs together with the core. The GUI then starts with everything already in place: the first frame is dark, with zero dialogs. Fail-safe: if the headless phase cannot settle within 15 minutes, the container falls back to the classic GUI installer (dialogs auto-confirmed by the agent, as before). Existing installs missing the theme extension are healed the same way.
- **New README banner wordmark.** "JDownloader" is set in Bree Serif, the house wordmark font (as on BombVault / ShipLog), instead of a generic Arial Black. Claim set in Lato, the shared claim font across all repos.
- **Opt-in geometry diagnostics.** Set `JD_DEBUG_GEO=1` to log the real pixel geometry around the speed graph (window, menubar, toolbar bounds, layout constraints, native and replacement graph) every ~5 seconds to the container log.
- **CI geometry probe.** A manually triggered workflow boots the built image, collects the geometry log lines, FlatLaf install forensics and a PNG screenshot of the live desktop as artifacts.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Theming: the official FlatLaf API instead of jar patching.** The `#161616` Carbon dark chrome now comes from FlatLaf's official `registerCustomDefaultsSource` API — the container registers its own colour file inside JD's JVM at runtime. JD's `flatlaf.jar` stays stock; the old mechanism (patching the jar and rewriting its SHA-256) is gone, so JD's integrity check is always satisfied and a JD self-update can no longer reset the theme. The colour values themselves are unchanged. Upgrades from earlier versions need no action.
- **Honest READY, ground truth everywhere.** The `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` banner fires only when the agent inside JD's JVM confirms the expected look-and-feel is actually applied, never from proxy signals like open ports or files on disk. If the theme cannot be verified within 10 minutes, the log says so honestly (`JDOWNLOADER IS UP (theme NOT verified)`) including the likely cause. The theme healer watches the applied look-and-feel, only acts after READY, and is rate-limited to 3 polite restarts per hour, so it can heal after weeks of uptime yet can never become a restart loop. A revision canary logs JD's exact core build on every launch, so drift after a self-update is diagnosable from the container log.
- **Process management follows JD by PID.** The launcher loop follows JD's self-update relaunches by PID (ground truth from the in-JVM agent) with a grace window and pgrep fallback, so a second instance on the same `/config` can no longer be spawned by a mis-detected relaunch. Repeated fast crashes back off exponentially instead of hammering a 5-second restart loop.
- Fresh installs now open the main window maximized and keep tracking the browser size (KasmVNC dynamic resize). Your own window-size choice is persisted by JD and never overwritten. The custom colour defaults are applied before JD builds its GUI, so every component is created dark from the start, and hot-swapping the theme on the live window (which could leave repaint artifacts) is gone.
- **Hardened bootstrap download.** The first-start download of `JDownloader.jar` is retried (3×) and validated as a real jar — a captive portal or DNS hijack serving an HTML page no longer ends up saved as the launcher. If all attempts fail, the log shows a loud, repeating error banner instead of exiting silently to an empty desktop.
- **Dialog agent hardening.** Dialog auto-confirm has per-window click guards (no rapid re-clicking), and the agent's state markers are wiped on every container boot and before every JD launch, so a crash-looping JD can't inherit stale "theme applied" state. Any JD dialog the agent doesn't recognise is logged once with its verbatim title and text, so a future forced dialog can be matched precisely instead of guessed from a screenshot.
- The v3 preview channel (`feat/v3` → `:v3-preview`) is retired now that v3 is released; if you tested the preview, switch the container back to `:latest`.
- CI icon-asset workflow no longer runs (and fails) on tag pushes.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Download graph: doubled in height, and rebuilt so it stays correct at any speed.** JDownloader hardcodes the toolbar row that holds the speed graph to 32px, with no config key — with the ads disabled, that corner looked cramped and half-empty. The bundled GUI agent raises that row to 64px at runtime (tool buttons stay centered, and the tweak survives JD's toolbar rebuilds and self-updates). Doubling the height also surfaced a real bug in JDownloader's graph painting (AppWork `Graph`): every sample is plotted as `(int)(height * value * 0.9) / max` with `value` in raw bytes/s — the `height * value` product is a 32-bit multiplication that overflows above ~34 MiB/s at the 64px row this image uses (~67 MiB/s even at JD's stock 32px). Overflowed samples wrap low or clip away entirely, and the speed-limit line vanishes (only its red text stays). The agent therefore hides the native speed meter and paints its own graph with 64-bit arithmetic: full height at any speed, same look (theme colours, average overlay, speed-limit band, localized texts). The native panel stays alive underneath, so its speed-limit menu keeps working (clicks are forwarded).
- **Speed graph clipped to half height.** JD's content pane grants the `dock NORTH` toolbar a strip measured before the agent grows the graph row, so the lower half of the 64px graph and of the buttons laid out for it was simply cut off. The agent now also pins the toolbar height in the content pane's component constraint (`height <pref>!`) and revalidates from the window. Verified in CI with real pixel geometry and on the box.
- **Toolbar row reverting after rebuilds.** JD's `updateToolbar()` installs a fresh MigLayout with the stock 32px row on every rebuild, which the earlier one-shot guard never re-grew. The row is now grown once per layout instance, and the hidden native speed meter is re-excluded from the layout (`hidemode 3`) after every rebuild so it can no longer reserve up to 300px of invisible width.
- **Speed-limit field clipped long values.** The speed-limit field in the Settings menu had a fixed width sized to fit only "500.00 KB/s" (JDownloader hardcodes it in `MenuEditor.getEditorWidth()`), so a higher limit such as "10,216 MiB/s" was cut off and unreadable. The bundled GUI agent now relaxes that fixed width and grows the menu so the whole value, including its unit, is shown.
- **White GUI after a clean install.** Two timing-dependent root causes, both fixed: `UIManager.setLookAndFeel(String)` resolves the LAF class through the system classloader, but JD's launcher wires `flatlaf.jar` only into its own classloader, so depending on boot timing the first GUI start could fail with `ClassNotFoundException` and fall back to the light default — the agent now appends `flatlaf.jar` to the system classloader through the official `Instrumentation.appendToSystemClassLoaderSearch` API. And the headless pre-install could be stopped while the updater was still writing `flatlaf.jar`, leaving a truncated jar that satisfied every "is it installed?" check and permanently blocked the theme — the pre-install settle gate now requires a zip-valid `flatlaf.jar` before the chain is stopped, a boot heal removes a corrupt jar and re-requests it, and the `JD_SELFUPDATE` freeze gate validates the jar instead of only checking that it exists. Existing broken installs repair themselves on the next container start; a Force Update is all that is needed.
- **The READY banner could lie.** It used to fire once JD's API port was up and the patched FlatLaf jar existed on disk, which says nothing about whether the theme was actually applied. The agent now records the actually-active look-and-feel, and `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` only prints when the expected theme is genuinely applied.

Every architectural claim in this release was verified empirically before shipping: the FlatLaf API signatures against the library's official signature file, the headless install behaviour and the extension pre-request in CI experiments on real JDownloader installs, an adversarial multi-agent review of the full diff, and the complete first-start and heal flows on a real Unraid box.
